A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Diamond Maps research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original posterior-sampling, image-recovery, SMC, and SANA-Sprint alignment experiments, including FID results, GenEval scores, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds ImageNet, FLUX, UniGenBench++, and held-out reward evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The two Diamond Map constructions remain. The stated distillation losses gain stop-gradient targets, Algorithm 2 adds ESS-triggered resampling and weight resets, and Algorithm 3 presents approximate, normalized guidance variants. The PDFs do not establish whether the newly documented practical heuristics changed the retained SANA experiments.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet1k at 256×256, including class-conditional generation, 32× super-resolution, and prompt-guided generation of unusual compositions. It also adds UniGenBench++ evaluation. CIFAR-10, CelebA, and GenEval coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens direct comparisons: DPS participates in new posterior-guidance and SMC evaluations, while Flow Map Guidance is compared with Weighted Diamond Maps on FLUX and in SANA qualitative examples. Table 1 also adds HyperNoise, explicitly sourcing that result from Eyring et al. (2025).

E3.justification: New experiments introduce FLUX sampling configurations, ImageNet SiT/CFG settings, KID evaluation, held-out reward protocols, and explicit compute accounting across model sizes. The retained CIFAR/CelebA training description changes the outer-time range from [0.01, 1.0] to [0.01, 0.99]; this reported revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds FLUX sensitivity analyses for noise, guidance frequency, and Monte Carlo samples; ImageNet analyses of sample allocation and SMC particle tradeoffs; and a held-out reward test of reward hacking. Existing SANA ablations and CelebA robustness analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figures 7 and 10 newly specify shared initial-noise seeds across qualitative comparisons, and Appendix D.1.4 discloses shared noise across SMC particles. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive ImageNet sampling, recovery, SMC, and prompt-alignment results, plus FLUX results reaching 0.785 on GenEval and 0.653 on UniGenBench++ in Figure 9. The original SANA mean GenEval score of 0.83 and CIFAR/CelebA FID table values remain unchanged. These are chiefly new-setting results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.9 adds a formal extension to general stochastic proposal operators, including change-of-variables and Jacobian-determinant terms and alternative proposal examples. The central consistency results, DDPM transition result, and their original proofs are substantially retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain largely stable. However, contribution 2 replaces the claim of optimal accuracy and efficiency with simple and effective estimation, and the new Discussion explicitly qualifies the ability to solve arbitrary reward-alignment problems.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the categorical posterior-versus-weighted efficiency comparison with reward-dependent importance-sampling reasoning and an open theoretical question. The new Discussion identifies large variance under poor prior coverage and errors inherited from imperfect distillation. New analyses also interpret reward hacking, Monte Carlo scaling, and excessive-noise failures.

D1.justification: v2 adds an experiment-code pointer, a FLUX checkpoint identifier, ImageNet architecture and initialization details, training configurations, sample counts, and NFE formulas. It also explains previously unspecified practical weighting, gradient normalization, and SANA score/velocity approximations. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility without establishing changes to every retained experiment.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Test-time Scaling of Diffusions with Flow Maps, Noise Hypernetworks, newer distillation methods, and the added datasets and benchmark. Section 6 removes the claim of being first to construct stochastic flow maps, while retaining most of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is extensively rewritten into implementation, model-specific analysis, and compute-scaling discussions. Appendix D is reorganized into separate dataset, guidance, SMC, normalization, and model subsections, and a new Discussion closes the paper. Most introductory and core theoretical exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial comparison grids, ablation panels, and ImageNet tables, and expands Tables 1 and 2. It incorporates v1 Figure 6 into the three-panel Figure 9. Existing displays are also relocated: v1 Figures 5, 7, and 8 become v2 Figures 17, 11, and 12.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical validation and sparse experimental documentation through ImageNet tests, FLUX and UniGenBench++ evaluations, direct guidance comparisons, and held-out reward analyses. Implementation disclosures and explicit variance and distillation limitations make the claims more assessable. Practical normalized guidance still differs from the proved estimator, and uncertainty reporting remains limited, but these gaps do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and reproducibility.
